title: Reference Types
learningObjectives: Explain the purpose and behavior of reference types in C#.
Choose an appropriate type for a simple application scenario.
Read and explain original C# code that demonstrates the lesson concepts.
Predict deterministic program output and identify common mistakes.
Compile and execute a small .NET 10 console example to verify the result.

understand.concept: A reference-type variable holds a reference to an object. Assigning that variable to another variable copies the reference, so both variables can refer to the same object. Classes, arrays, delegates and strings are reference types; reference variables can also have a null value.
understand.whyItMatters: Understanding references helps explain shared mutable state, object identity and null-related bugs.
understand.analogy: A reference is like two notes containing the same locker number: both notes point to the same locker.
understand.analogyLimit: A reference is not a human-readable locker number and the analogy does not describe garbage collection or memory addresses.

explain.narrative:
## Reference-type variables

A variable of a reference type stores a reference to an object rather than an inline copy of the object's data. Class instances and arrays are common examples. The string type is also a reference type, although strings are immutable.

## Copying a reference

When a reference variable is assigned to another variable, the reference is copied. Both variables can then access the same object. Mutating that object through one reference is observable through the other.

## Null references

A reference can be null, meaning it does not currently refer to an object. Nullable reference annotations such as string? help communicate this possibility to the compiler; they do not create a different runtime reference type.

## Baseline

Examples target .NET 10 and C# 14. Reference identity is distinct from value equality.

questions.prompt: What does assigning one array variable to another copy?
options: Every array element into a new array
questions.explanation: Reference assignment copies the reference; it does not clone the array.

questions.prompt: Which operation creates a new class instance?
questions.explanation: The new operator creates an instance and returns a reference to it.

questions.prompt: What does null indicate for a reference variable?
questions.answer: It does not currently refer to an object
options: It does not currently refer to an object
It has been garbage-collected for certain
questions.explanation: null represents the absence of an object reference.

questions.prompt: Which type is a reference type?
questions.explanation: Array types are reference types, even when their elements are value types.

questions.prompt: What does string? mean with nullable reference types enabled?
questions.answer: The reference is allowed to be null
options: The reference is allowed to be null
The string stores a nullable value type
The runtime creates a new string wrapper
questions.explanation: The nullable annotation communicates that the reference may be null.
